recent_posts.title: GitHub - lsdrfrx/telegram_ex: Elixir library for building Telegram bots with macro-based API
recent_posts.summary: TelegramEx is an Elixir library for building Telegram bots using a macro-based API inspired by GenServer patterns. It supports stateless and stateful (FSM-based) message handlers, pipeline-style message builders for text, photos, documents, stickers, videos, locations, and contacts, inline and reply keyboards, callback query handling, and router modules for organizing handlers by domain. The library integrates with OTP supervision trees and handles forum topics automatically. A roadmap outlines planned features including webhooks, middlewares, rate limiting, and message editing.

recent_posts.title: Hologram UI
recent_posts.summary: Hologram UI is an upcoming official component library for the Hologram framework. It offers accessible, responsive, cross-browser-compatible components designed around Hologram's conventions, with a consistent API, shared design tokens, and reusable composition patterns. The library aims to save developers from rebuilding common UI building blocks and will be offered at an affordable price, with proceeds supporting the Hologram project.

recent_posts.title: Deploy a Phoenix app to a VPS using Potions.io
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of deploying a Phoenix app to a VPS using Potions.io, a deployment tool built by the author that handles zero-downtime releases, SSL, PostgreSQL provisioning, environment variables, and migrations automatically. The tutorial covers creating a new Phoenix app, preparing it for release with mix phx.gen.release, pushing to GitHub, and deploying via Potions. It also demonstrates using Tidewave (an AI coding assistant for Elixir) to build a memory-style guessing game, then shipping updates via auto-deploy on git push. Key Potions features highlighted include preview domains, custom domain support with automatic SSL, scheduled database backups, and an in-browser remote IEx console.

recent_posts.title: Thinking Elixir Podcast 302: BEAM in Your Pocket
recent_posts.summary: Episode 302 of the Thinking Elixir podcast covers several Elixir ecosystem news items: Folio, a new library for generating print-quality PDFs/SVGs/PNGs from Markdown using a Rust NIF; Mob, an early-stage framework for building native mobile apps with Elixir targeting Android (Compose) and iOS (SwiftUI); Oban 2.22 and Oban Pro 1.7 releases with job querying improvements, workflow tracking tables, and new signal/await job pause-resume functionality; LiveView Vue 1.1 with a new QuickBeam-based nodeless SSR mode; ExAst, a new library for structural search and code modification over Elixir ASTs; Erlang QUIC 1.3 reaching its first production-ready release as a pure Erlang HTTP/3 implementation; and Spinnel, an experimental compiled Ruby tool by Matz capable of 86x speedups and native binary compilation.

recent_posts.title: Getting Started — ExRatatui v0.8.2
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step getting started guide for ExRatatui v0.8.2, an Elixir terminal UI library wrapping Ratatui via NIFs. Covers project setup, the bare-metal API (draw, poll_event, terminal_size), the ExRatatui.App behaviour with mount/render/handle_event callbacks, layout splitting with constraints, styling and rich text with Span/Line, and culminates in a fully functional supervised todo app featuring TextInput, List widgets, and focus management between panels. Also points to further guides on SSH/distribution transports, testing, performance, and custom widgets.

recent_posts.title: GitHub - mcass19/kino_ex_ratatui: Run ExRatatui apps inside Livebook
recent_posts.summary: KinoExRatatui is an Elixir library that enables running ExRatatui terminal UI apps inside Livebook notebooks. It works as a byte-stream transport that pipes ANSI output through xterm.js embedded in a Livebook cell, while forwarding keypresses and resize events back to the app. Features include responsive sizing via xterm.js FitAddon, static frame rendering for documentation, and zero browser-side state on cell re-evaluation. The library supports both callback and reducer runtimes, with example notebooks for a system monitor dashboard, a mock AI chat interface, and a counter app.

recent_posts.title: Release v0.9.0 · elixir-error-tracker/error-tracker
recent_posts.summary: Version 0.9.0 of the elixir-error-tracker library has been released. New features include occurrence data in error telemetry events. Fixes cover improved sensitive header redaction, propagation of the muted flag to :error telemetry events, and resolution of compilation warnings on Elixir 1.20. The release also replaces the credo linter with styler and expands the test matrix to include Elixir 1.20.x.

recent_posts.title: GitHub - m1dnight/ferri: A self-hostable HTTP tunnel. Expose your local dev server to the internet with a single command.
recent_posts.summary: Ferri is an open-source, self-hostable HTTP tunnel similar to ngrok that exposes local dev servers to the internet via a free SSL-terminating endpoint. It provides a single-binary client installable via curl, generates random human-readable URLs, and handles SSL termination at the host. The backend is built with Elixir/Phoenix using the Yamux protocol, while the client is written in Rust. Self-hosting requires a VPS, wildcard domain, and a reverse proxy like Caddy. Full setup instructions are provided including SystemD service configuration, Caddy wildcard TLS setup with Gandi DNS, and UFW firewall rules.

recent_posts.title: Thinking Elixir Podcast 301: Testing, Debugging, and Departures
recent_posts.summary: Episode 301 of the Thinking Elixir podcast covers several community updates: Phoenix Live Debugger hits 1.0 with an interactive tour, LiveStash 0.2 releases to solve Phoenix LiveView state loss during WebSocket reconnections, a free Phoenix testing course at testingliveview.com becomes available, Volt 0.8 (an Elixir-native frontend build tool) is released, and Francisco Sesarini departs Erlang Solutions. Hosts also discuss how LLMs are changing developer education and the ethics of AI training data.

recent_posts.title: The Broker Evaluation Gauntlet: Four Futures APIs Compared
recent_posts.summary: A developer who integrated four futures broker APIs (IBKR, TradeStation, Tradovate, ThinkOrSwim) into the same Elixir trading system shares a practical evaluation framework. The post covers authentication complexity (OAuth2 vs custom flows), symbol convention differences across brokers, streaming protocols (SSE vs WebSocket), order execution reliability, and operational concerns like session management and environment parity. IBKR was removed after silent stop order failures. The author's priority order for broker evaluation puts authentication complexity and order execution reliability above commission rates or platform features.

top_posts.title: Embracing raw SQL over ORMs with type safe code generation
top_posts.summary: Explores an alternative approach to database access that embraces raw SQL instead of abstracting it away with ORMs. Introduces Squirrel, a library for Gleam that uses code generation from SQL queries to provide type-safety and good developer experience without sacrificing performance. Demonstrates how developers can write plain SQL while maintaining the benefits of static typing in functional languages, avoiding common ORM pitfalls like N+1 query problems.

top_posts.title: Fine-Tuning YOLO to Watch Soccer Matches
top_posts.summary: Fine-tuning pre-trained YOLO models for specialized object detection tasks requires significantly less data and training time than building from scratch. Using a soccer dataset with 7,010 training images, the author demonstrates how to adapt a COCO-trained YOLOv11 model to detect balls, players, referees, and goalkeepers with 88% mAP50 accuracy. The process involves using Ultralytics tools for training, monitoring key metrics like loss values and mAP50, and converting the final PyTorch model to ONNX format for deployment in Elixir applications. The fine-tuned model shows superior contextual understanding compared to generic models, focusing on field action while filtering out background spectators.

top_posts.title: Elixir → JavaScript Porting Initiative
top_posts.summary: Hologram needs community help porting 171 Erlang standard library functions to JavaScript to enable Elixir execution in browsers. The project is 34% complete for Phase 1, which focuses on full-stack web applications. Contributors don't need deep Erlang knowledge - just basic JavaScript and Elixir skills to follow existing patterns. Tasks range from 15 minutes to a few hours, and AI tools are encouraged. Each ported function unlocks multiple Elixir stdlib functions, creating a multiplier effect for the community.

top_posts.title: Lazy Doc, Your documentation tool has arrived.
top_posts.summary: Lazy Doc is an AI-powered tool designed to generate documentation for Elixir functions that lack it. By analyzing the source code, it identifies undocumented public functions and creates documentation automatically. It also offers features like documentation checking for CI pipelines, private function handling, and AST manipulation to maintain code format. The tool aims to enforce documentation practices while making the process easier and more efficient.

top_posts.title: Overengineered #001: Hello World
top_posts.summary: The post explores building an overengineered 'Hello World' system using Elixir. It demonstrates creating a distributed system where multiple nodes automatically discover each other and send 'hello world' messages to newly joined nodes. The setup involves using GenServers, UDP broadcast for node discovery, and handling node greetings with the Greeter module. The project is aimed at learning and fun, showcasing an extensive approach to a simple problem.
